title: The Record High Diesel Prices
gist: Diesel prices are hitting new nominal all-time highs on soaring crack spreads, pushing the US price above $5/gallon and higher across the OECD; even though real prices remain below the 2008, 2011-12 and 2022 peaks, Gavekal frames sustained high diesel as a direct tax on trucking, farming, shipping, mining and construction because economic activity is fundamentally energy transformed.

themes.theme: Diesel's Nominal Highs vs. Real History

insights.claim: Diesel prices around the world are making new all-time highs in nominal terms because of soaring crack spreads.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A nominal all-time-high diesel price is a fresh cost shock for transport- and energy-intensive sectors regardless of the real-terms comparison.

insights.claim: In real terms, today's diesel prices remain below the 2008 peak (driven by China's post-earthquake shift to diesel generators), the 2011-2012 peak (driven by the Fukushima-triggered nuclear shutdowns in Japan and Germany), and the 2022 spike that followed the start of the Ukraine war.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: The nominal high looks less alarming once deflated, tempering comparisons to past energy-shock recessions.

insights.claim: The US diesel price is now above $5/gallon in real terms, and it is even higher across most of the OECD.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A $5/gallon threshold breached across the OECD, not just the US, signals a broad-based rather than country-specific cost shock to monitor.

themes.theme: Diesel as a Tax on the Real Economy

insights.claim: Above $5/gallon, diesel prices materially raise the cost of trucking, farming, shipping, mining and construction, squeezing broad swaths of the real economy.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Watch input costs and margins in logistics, agriculture, and heavy industry as a diesel-driven drag rather than isolated sector weakness.
insights.locator: And above US$5/gallon, few good things happen

insights.claim: Because economic activity is fundamentally energy transformed, large parts of the economy generate activity and profits far more easily when diesel prices are low than when they are high.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Use sustained high diesel/energy prices as a standing headwind on corporate margins and GDP growth, not a transient input-cost blip.
insights.locator: As we never tire of pointing out, "economic activity is energy transformed"
